findings.title: CMEK-encrypted Dataflow job has no companion IAM grant for the Dataflow service agent or the worker service account on its KMS key
findings.explanation: module.dataflow.tf wires kms_key_name = google_kms_crypto_key.main.id into the Dataflow job, and HLD_GCP_215 passes because kms_key_name is set. But Cloud Dataflow validates CMEK access at apply/first-use time, not at plan time, and requires TWO separate grants of roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the key: (1) the Dataflow Service Agent (service-PROJECT_NUMBER@dataflow-service-producer-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com), and (2) the job's controller/worker service account. Neither grant existed anywhere in this repo. Terraform applies cleanly and the job creation call fails with a permission-denied error from the Dataflow API. This is the same class of gap already codified for Healthcare (HLD_GCP_482) and Document AI (HLD_GCP_476), but no equivalent policy exists yet for google_dataflow_job, and HLD_GCP_215/216 (the two policies that do cover this resource type) don't check for it. The shipped HLD_GCP_483 policy (PR pending) only checks grant (1) — expressing grant (2) deterministically is harder in general since the expected grantee depends on whether service_account_email is set. As a follow-up to this finding, var.service_account_email was made a required (no-default) module variable, with a validation rule rejecting the default Compute Engine SA pattern outright, so grant (2)'s target is always a caller-supplied dedicated SA rather than the broad default SA — closing the gap at the module level rather than relying on policy coverage alone.
findings.remediation: Add a data "google_project" source and two google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member grants of roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on google_kms_crypto_key.main: one to the Dataflow Service Agent, one to the job's controller service account.

suggested_policies.rationale: Dataflow jobs configured with kms_key_name pass HLD_GCP_215 (kms_key_name not_null) but the Dataflow Service Agent still needs an explicit roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter grant on that key before the API will actually use it — Terraform accepts the config, GCP rejects it at apply/first-use time. This mirrors the already-shipped HLD_GCP_476 (Document AI) and HLD_GCP_482 (Cloud Healthcare) policies for google_document_ai_processor and google_healthcare_dataset respectively; google_dataflow_job has no equivalent yet.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_001
name: Dataflow jobs using CMEK must grant the Dataflow service agent key access
principle: encryption
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  Cloud Dataflow validates that the Dataflow Service Agent
  (service-PROJECT_NUMBER@dataflow-service-producer-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com)
  holds roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on a job's CMEK key before
  it will use that key. Terraform accepts the configuration without this
  grant; only the GCP control plane rejects it, at apply or first-use time,
  which makes the gap easy to miss until deployment.
remediation: |
  ```hcl
  data "google_project" "current" {}

  resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member" "dataflow_service_agent" {
    crypto_key_id = google_kms_crypto_key.main.id
    role          = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
    member        = "serviceAccount:service-${data.google_project.current.number}@dataflow-service-producer-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_dataflow_job:
    filter:
      path: kms_key_name
      not_null: true
    any:
      - requires_companion:
          type: google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member
          linked_via:
            from: kms_key_name
            to: crypto_key_id
          where:
            path: role
            equals: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
      - requires_companion:
          type: google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding
          linked_via:
            from: kms_key_name
            to: crypto_key_id
          where:
            path: role
            equals: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
